channel.title: The Retreat Register — Updates
channel.description: Verification progress from The Retreat Register, published with real numbers: coverage snapshots, data findings, and what gets cut from the register and why.

item.title: Hotel Attrition Allowance: How Planners Read It Before Signing
item.description: What the attrition allowance in a room block contract means, and how to tell whether it counts per night or over the whole stay.

item.title: How to Plan a Board Retreat: Set the Objectives, Then Pick the Room
item.description: Plan a board retreat from its objectives: agree them with the chair and the chief executive, then choose the agenda and the room.

item.title: Leadership Retreat Topics: Choose the Few the Team Must Decide
item.description: How to pick leadership retreat topics the team must decide together, and keep the list shorter than the days allow.

item.title: Team Retreat Agenda: Build a Two-Day Schedule With Free Time
item.description: A two-day team retreat agenda with focused mornings, free afternoons and one shared evening, plus who runs each block.

item.title: Hiring a DJ for a Company Offsite: What Planners Ask the Venue
item.description: Before booking a DJ, planners ask the venue about noise curfews, outside vendors and the insurance a vendor must show.

item.title: Retreat Center Insurance: What Owners Carry Before Hosting Groups
item.description: The cover a retreat center holds before groups arrive, and the proof of insurance owners ask each renting group to send.

item.title: Retreat ROI: Build the One-Page Report Planners Send to Leadership
item.description: Show leadership what a retreat achieved. Pick one or two outcomes before the trip, log each decision and its owner, and send a one-page report within two weeks.

item.title: Team Retreat Activities: Choose by Goal and Check the Venue Can Host Them
item.description: An activity earns its place on the agenda when it serves the retreat's goal. How to pick by purpose, and the venue questions each kind of activity raises.

item.title: Build a Retreat Planning Timeline That Works Backward From the Date
item.description: A retreat has a planned arrival date and a long list of tasks with their own deadlines. A backward-planned checklist, grouped by phase, for first-time organizers.

item.title: Drive-To Retreats From New York City: Compare the Catskills, Hudson Valley, and Poconos
item.description: Three regions sit within a drive of New York City and suit different teams. How to compare them on travel, setting, and the kind of property each one offers.

item.title: Corporate Retreats in the North Carolina Mountains: Choose a Base Town First
item.description: In the North Carolina mountains, the base town shapes the trip. How airport access, elevation, and season should steer a company's choice of base.

item.title: Glamping or Cabins? Choose the Right Lodging for Your Group Retreat
item.description: Canvas tents and cabins can sit on the same property and suit very different groups. A side-by-side look at weather, bathrooms, sleep, and working space.

item.title: How to Host a Silent Retreat: Choose a Venue That Can Hold the Quiet
item.description: A loud, shared, or conversation-centered venue works against a silent retreat. The property checks that matter before a teacher or organizer books.

item.title: Types of Retreats: Match the Format to the Goal Before You Search
item.description: Corporate, wellness, silent, creative, faith-based, and family retreats ask different things of a venue. A guide to the main formats and what to check for each.

item.title: Define a Corporate Retreat Before You Search for Venues
item.description: A corporate retreat takes a team away from the office, usually overnight, for focused work. A plain definition, and how the goal shapes the venue search.

item.title: How to Negotiate a Retreat Venue Quote in One Polite Email
item.description: A venue quote has more parts than the rate. The terms worth asking about, how to put them in one written request, and how to keep the tone friendly.

item.title: How to Check a Venue Booking Before You Send a Deposit
item.description: Look-alike venue listings exist, and a deposit is hard to get back. The desk checks that take minutes, and the payment habits that protect the group.

item.title: How to Ask to Move a Retreat Date and Put the Terms in Writing
item.description: A date change is a different request from a cancellation. How to ask for one, and what to get in writing.

item.title: Retreat Cancellation Clauses: Read the Date-Based Charges Before You Sign
item.description: Some venue contracts charge more to cancel as the date gets closer. How a sliding scale works and which terms are worth asking about.

item.title: The Food and Beverage Minimum: Know What Your Group Must Spend
item.description: A food and beverage minimum is the least a group agrees to spend on catering. What counts toward it, what does not, and what happens if the group falls short.
